name: Value Proposition Fit Matrix (Relievers vs. Pains)
phase: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that our core value proposition outranks existing market alternatives on speed and clarity. We will verify this by presenting a relative comparison matrix to 12 prospective users, and consider it validated if ≥ 70% prioritize our specific pain relievers over incumbent alternatives.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Build a two-sided canvas that maps pain relievers to customer pains and gain creators to gains.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Have target users rate each element’s clarity, relevance and difference against their current alternative.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Score fit with a weighted model calibrated to the pains users ranked highest.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Build a two-sided Value Proposition Canvas explicitly mapping Pain Relievers to Customer Pains and Gain Creators to Customer Gains.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Conduct structured review sessions where target users evaluate the clarity, relevance, and differentiation of each value proposition element against their current operational alternatives.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Quantify the fit score using a weighted distribution model calibrated to user-prioritized pain points.

warning.label: Theoretical Value Congruence
warning.text: A proposition can read as cohesive and compelling on paper and still not move anyone off the incumbent.

warningFull: A value proposition can appear conceptually cohesive and compelling on paper while failing to generate sufficient switching momentum to overcome incumbent inertia.

origin.title: Value Proposition Design: How to Create Products and Services Customers Want
